equity_bridge.item: Series A 10.25% perpetual preferred stock at liquidation preference

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal load growth plus capacity additions; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-24% 3yr, 0% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+27.6% 5yr) and EPS (+14.1% 5yr) by far more than 30pp. Book equity is shrunk by buybacks and mark-to-market swings and then tripled in Q1-2026 by the stock issued for the LS Power portfolio; revenue 5yr CAGR is the 2021 Direct Energy acquisition. None of these is a growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 and FY2020 annuals. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2020 1,553, FY2022 -47, FY2025 540; the 3yr CAGR is undefined from a negative base. Reported FCF fell from 1,607 to 766 over five years while SBC plus award taxes rose from 54 to 226, so owner FCF fell faster than reported FCF. FY2025 capex (1,147) includes the Texas Development Projects.

scenario_narratives.base: The enlarged fleet earns roughly what FY2026 guidance implies. FY2027 gets a full year of the LS Power portfolio and PJM capacity at the $329-333/MW-day cap; Cedar Bayou 5 and Greens Bayou 6 come on in mid-2028 and the first data-center agreements (295 MW signed, a path to ~1 GW) contribute from 2028-29, taking Adjusted EBITDA from ~5.6B to ~6.2B. From there the margin fades to 15.0% as capacity prices come off the cap once the price collar lapses and retail margins give some of the 2024-26 expansion back. Vivint keeps growing subscribers at a mid-single-digit rate and keeps costing ~0.9B a year net to do it. Federal NOLs shelter most cash tax through FY2029, then the rate is 24%. Growth capex drops from ~0.8B in FY2027 to ~0.25B a year. Leverage falls through free cash flow and the asset sale, which is treated as value-neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: The data-center thesis delivers. 'Bring Your Own Power' contracts scale toward the 6 GW ambition (the reported 1.2-2.4 GW hyperscaler project starts in late 2029, GE Vernova/Kiewit slots are used), ERCOT peak demand tracks the 139 GW 2030 forecast, and PJM capacity stays tight after the collar. Adjusted EBITDA reaches ~8B by FY2031 and ~9.2B by FY2036, with a rising contracted share. The cost is a decade of heavy capex (8-9% of revenue through FY2030, ~$11B more than base), so free cash flow stays below the base case until FY2032 and the value sits in the terminal year. Integration of the LS Power fleet goes to plan and leverage is not a constraint.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns while the balance sheet is stretched. PJM capacity prices fall back toward historical levels once the cap/floor mechanism expires after the 2027/28 auction, gas-fired spark spreads compress, hyperscaler commitments slip so the data-center pipeline does not convert, retail margins are squeezed by supply costs and by affordability legislation of the Maryland SB 1 kind, and Vivint loses share to DIY and telecom bundles while its acquisition cost stays fixed. Adjusted EBITDA falls from ~5.5B to ~4.6B by FY2030 and only grows with inflation afterwards. With net debt near 23B, a 20% fall in EBITDA takes roughly 60% off the equity value; refinancing costs and collateral calls would add pressure that the unlevered model does not capture.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NRG is valued as an operating company on unlevered owner free cash flow built from Adjusted EBITDA guidance, with the two costs that measure leaves out (stock compensation including withholding taxes, and Vivint's capitalized subscriber costs) charged in full, the NOL tax shield run off over three years, and margins faded to mid-cycle before a 13x terminal multiple is applied. Net debt and the preferred are then deducted. Because debt is about half of enterprise value, the equity is a levered claim: small changes in EBITDA, the multiple or the discount rate move the per-share value roughly twice as much, and the three scenarios are deliberately wide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: net debt 22.9B plus 650 preferred against ~5.6B Adjusted EBITDA; each 0.5x turn of terminal multiple is roughly $8 per share in the base case
PJM capacity prices cleared at the FERC cap for 2026/27 and 2027/28; the base case fades margins only modestly afterwards

Adjusted EBITDA to cash bridge: the capitalized contract cost charge (~850-900/yr net) is derived from balance-sheet rolls and the guidance bridge, not from a published reconciliation in the extracted filings
Divested EBITDA of the 4.9 GW sale is undisclosed; the sale is assumed value-neutral and must be re-anchored at close (target Q2-2027)
Revenue is largely commodity pass-through, so margin-on-revenue paths are a vehicle for EBITDA dollars; a gas-price move changes revenue without changing value
Data-center growth capex in the bull case is an estimate; no project-level economics are disclosed
ARO and pension deficits are not in the bridge

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 79.65-189.96
data_sources.financials: NRG_Metrics.csv; NRG_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (balance sheet, cash flow, debt note, capex table, NOL and tax disclosure, held-for-sale note); NRG_Annual_FY2025.txt (cash flow statement, interest income, capitalized contract costs)
data_sources.qualitative: NRG_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 guidance, LS Power acquisition and partial sale-back, data-center strategy, bull and bear cases

inputs.share_count_basis: 209.98M common shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet; includes the 24.25M shares issued to LS Power on 2026-01-30) plus ~1M outstanding equity-compensation instruments (10-Q EPS note). Q3-2026 diluted weighted average was 210M. Held FLAT because SBC and the cash tax withheld on award settlement are both expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-09-30 from cash flow statements (FY2025 10-K + 9M-2026 less 9M-2025 10-Q): amortization of unearned equity compensation 160 (134 - 83 + 109) plus 'equivalent shares purchased in lieu of tax withholdings' 107 (92 - 86 + 101) in financing. The two lines are summed because the 10-K/10-Q publish no combined figure.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-yr UST), ERP ~5%, levered beta ~1.1 for a merchant generator/retailer -> cost of equity ~9.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6% (recent senior notes 5.75%, 3% TEF loans, 10.25% preferred), ~4.6% after tax. At current market weights (~47% equity / 53% debt) that is ~7.0%; at the deleveraged target structure (~60/40) ~7.8%. 8.0% is used for all three scenarios: cyclicality, commodity and integration risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in a per-scenario WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost is already inside EBITDA, so operating lease liabilities (207 at 2026-09-30) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases (45) are inside total_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest. The 650 Series A 10.25% perpetual preferred (liquidation preference) is deducted in equity_bridge; its dividends (~67/yr) are not in the unlevered flows.
inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E revenue = 9M-2026 actual 27,203 + Q4 estimate ~9,300 (Q4-2025 was 7,753 before the LS Power portfolio). FY0 is the guidance year rather than FY2025 because FY2025 pre-dates the acquisition that doubled the fleet, and because the 2026-09-30 net debt already reflects nine months of FY2026 cash flow; year 1 of the build is FY2027.
inputs.net_debt_note: total_debt is principal from the Q3-2026 10-Q debt note: recourse 21,337 + Lightning non-recourse 1,715 + finance leases 45 = 23,097 (carrying value on the balance sheet 22,923). Cash 148 excludes restricted cash (29) and counterparty deposits (105). FY2025 year-end cash of 4,708 was acquisition pre-funding and is gone.
inputs.pending_sale_treatment: The 2026-11-09 agreement to sell 4.9 GW back to LS Power for $4B cash (target close Q2-2027; HSR/FERC/NYSPSC) is NOT pro-formaed: the assets stay in the flows and the debt stays in net debt. The filings do not disclose the divested EBITDA. Pro-rating the January purchase suggests ~$450-550M, i.e. a sale at ~7-9x against the model's own ~8x implied EV/EBITDA, so the sale is approximately value-neutral in this model. Two caveats: NRG expects a $400-600M impairment (mostly goodwill) on held-for-sale classification in Q4-2026, meaning the price is below January carrying value; and the $1B of proceeds earmarked for buybacks is value-neutral here by construction. Re-anchor net debt, shares and the EBITDA path when the sale closes.
inputs.adjusted_ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is on NRG's Adjusted EBITDA guidance basis (FY2026 $5,325-5,825M, midpoint 5,575 = 15.3% of FY2026E revenue). That measure adds back SBC and excludes the cash spent on capitalized contract costs (mostly Vivint subscriber acquisition and fulfilment). Both are charged here: SBC through sbc_pct_path; contract costs through capex_pct_path. Capitalized contract cost cash spend is derived from the balance-sheet roll: FY2025 1,220 -> 1,680 plus 510 amortization = ~970; 9M-2026 1,680 -> 2,100 plus 511 amortization = ~930 (~1,200 annualized). Net of the fulfilment amortization already expensed inside cost of operations (~300/yr) the charge is ~850-900/yr. The exact Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation is published in the earnings releases, which are not in Extracted/; the bridge was cross-checked against guidance instead: 5,575 EBITDA - 3,050 FCFbG = 2,525 = interest ~1,250 + cash tax ~90 + maintenance/environmental capex 481 + net contract costs and other ~700.
inputs.tax_note: Federal NOL carryforwards of $6.6B gross at 2025-12-31 ($1.4B tax-effected at 2026-09-30); management expects net cash tax payments of up to $90M in 2026. The cash tax path ramps 6% -> 10% -> 18% -> 24% (21% federal + state) so the unlevered model consumes roughly the $1.4B tax-effected shield over FY2027-FY2029 and none after. The NOL is NOT also added in equity_bridge.
inputs.not_in_bridge: Asset retirement obligations and pension/OPEB deficits (inside 889 of other non-current liabilities) are not deducted; derivative assets and liabilities are treated as net operating hedges. Together these are a modest unquantified overstatement.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical adaptations (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). NRG is an operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow (retail energy, merchant generation, Vivint subscriptions); none of the non-FCF rows of the routing table applies, and the announced asset sale is a partial disposal, not a takeover of NRG, so the three-scenario frame holds. Cyclical adaptations applied: (1) FY0 is the FY2026 guidance year, not the last audited year; (2) EBITDA margin in the base case fades from 15.3-15.5% to a 15.0% mid-cycle level rather than capitalizing PJM capacity prices that cleared at the FERC cap; (3) terminal cap multiple of 13x unlevered owner FCF (~7x EBITDA) instead of the 20x compounder default, and it binds in every scenario (Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x); (4) one WACC for all scenarios. last_fcf/reported_fcf are TTM to 2026-09-30 LEVERED figures (OCF 2,168 - capex 1,479 = 689, after ~1.1B of interest and ~1B of growth capex) kept for auditability; the forward build is unlevered and starts from Adjusted EBITDA. interest_income is 0 because the company is heavily net-debt. BUYBACKS: funded repurchaser - 1,326 TTM (1,311 - 958 + 973), far above SBC, so the flat count is paid for; 9M-2026 repurchases were made at an average $154.45. LEVERAGE: net debt is ~52% of enterprise value, so each 1% of EV is ~2% of equity value; scenario spread and the hurdle-rate entry price are dominated by this. The entry price at a 15% hurdle is close to zero because debt absorbs almost all of the enterprise value at that discount rate - a finding about leverage, not an error.

bear.capex_note: Committed Texas builds finish; growth capex stops; maintenance and Vivint contract costs (~1.45B) do not shrink with margins.

base.capex_note: PP&E maintenance + environmental ~500-550/yr, net capitalized contract costs ~850-900/yr, plus growth: ~800 in FY2027 (Cedar Bayou 5 and Greens Bayou 6, COD mid-2028, and LS Power integration), ~400 in FY2028, then ~250/yr of sustaining growth.
base.narrative: FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA ~5.75B (full year of the LS Power fleet, PJM capacity at the cap), ~6.2B by FY2029 as the Texas builds and first data-center contracts arrive, then margin fades to a 15.0% mid-cycle level; EBITDA ~7.0B by FY2036.

bull.capex_note: Roughly $11B of capex above the base case over ten years, buying ~$2.2B of incremental FY2036 EBITDA (new gas build for data-center contracts plus higher power and capacity prices on the existing fleet).
bull.terminal_cap_note: 15x rather than 13x because in this scenario a quarter or more of EBITDA is under 15-20 year contracts; still below the 17x Gordon value.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: net debt is ~4.1x FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA after a debt-funded acquisition that is already being partly reversed at a loss to carrying value, there have been two consecutive adjusted-EPS misses and a CEO change in 2026, and base-case margins rest on PJM capacity prices at a regulatory cap. Base 50%: guidance has been reaffirmed through both misses and the asset sale gives a credible deleveraging path. Bull cut to 25%: it needs hyperscaler contracts to convert at scale, turbines and construction to arrive on time and on budget, and capacity markets to stay tight after the collar - several independent things.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
